hardWonKnowledge: INNER TIMEOUT SHORTER THAN OUTER — the same invariant apple-notes encodes for AppleScript, re-derived here for MapKit, with the SAME 5-second gap: `static let asyncTimeoutSeconds: TimeInterval = 15` (apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/apple_maps_bridge.swift:41) against `self.timeout_seconds = 20` (apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/maps_bridge.py:23). Swift races the MapKit call against a Task.sleep inside a throwing task group and cancelAll()s the loser (swift:204-225), so the helper emits a structured SEARCH_TIMEOUT/DIRECTIONS_TIMEOUT JSON error and exits cleanly instead of being SIGKILLed mid-call. CAVEAT THE KERNEL MUST FIX RATHER THAN COPY: the 15s bound is PER MAPKIT OPERATION, not per process. The `directions` command runs three sequentially — resolveFirstMapItem(origin) swift:99, resolveFirstMapItem(destination) swift:100, directions.calculate() swift:108-114 — so worst case is 45s inside a 20s outer timeout and the invariant is violated exactly when it matters most. The kernel should hand the child a single absolute deadline, not a per-call constant.

COMPILE-ON-FIRST-USE WITH AN MTIME STALENESS GATE — `if self.helper_binary.exists() and self.helper_binary.stat().st_mtime >= self.helper_source.stat().st_mtime: return` (apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/maps_bridge.py:36). This is the entire build system. Intent is documented in apple-maps/start.sh:4-5: "The Swift Maps helper is compiled on first use (swiftc). Editing files under this folder takes effect on the next launch — no manual build step." Without the mtime comparison every tool call pays a multi-second `swiftc -O`; without the rebuild leg, editing the .swift file silently does nothing. Verified live: source mtime Jul 29 11:58, binary mtime Jul 29 12:18, so no rebuild fires.

`swiftc -parse-as-library` IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT COSMETIC — apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/maps_bridge.py:40: `["swiftc", "-parse-as-library", "-O", str(self.helper_source), "-o", str(self.helper_binary)]`. The helper is a single .swift file using `@main struct AppleMapsBridge` with `static func main() async` (swift:39-48). A lone .swift file compiled WITHOUT -parse-as-library is treated as top-level script code and swiftc then rejects @main. Anyone tidying this flag list reintroduces a hard compile failure that surfaces as the near-useless HELPER_COMPILE_FAILED. There is no comment explaining this — the knowledge exists only in the argv array.

BUILD ARTIFACT IS DELIBERATELY WRITTEN OUTSIDE THE REPO, AND IS THE SERVER'S ONLY ENV ESCAPE HATCH — apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/config.py:31-36 resolves the build dir from `APPLE_MAPS_MCP_HELPER_BUILD_DIR`, defaulting to `~/.apple-mcps/build`. Directly relevant to the post-mortem: had the binary been emitted next to the .swift source, a repo under ~/Documents would have been denied the WRITE as well as the read. A grep across the monorepo (excluding node_modules/.venv/.git) finds exactly ONE reference to `apple-mcps` — this config.py line — so the deliberately generic directory name is aspirational; no other server shares it. The kernel should adopt this path and make it genuinely shared.

STRUCTURED ERROR CODES FROM THE HELPER ARE SILENTLY DISCARDED — a live bug, and a requirement for the kernel design. Swift emits a full envelope on stderr then exits 1 via writeErrorAndExit (apple_maps_bridge.swift:227-233). Python catches it at apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/maps_bridge.py:76-78: `stderr = exc.stderr.strip() or exc.stdout.strip()` / `raise MapsBridgeError("HELPER_FAILED", stderr or "Apple Maps helper failed.", "Retry the request.")` — it never json.loads() the stderr. Result: PLACE_NOT_FOUND, ROUTE_NOT_FOUND, SEARCH_TIMEOUT, DIRECTIONS_TIMEOUT, INVALID_INPUT and UNKNOWN_COMMAND all reach the model as error_code HELPER_FAILED with a raw JSON string as the message, and the actionable suggestion the helper computed is thrown away. The kernel needs a first-class 'child process speaks a structured error envelope' contract on BOTH sides.

PARTIAL FAILURE IS A FIRST-CLASS RESULT, NOT AN EXCEPTION — the only substantive explanatory comment in the server, apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/tools.py:158-159: "Prices a single origin→destination leg, returning a failed option rather than raising so one bad address cannot sink a whole comparison." Backed by TravelOption.ok / TravelOption.error (models.py:59, :66-68), the succeeded/failed counters on TravelMatrixResponse (tools.py:249-251), and reused by maps_check_campus_hops (tools.py:336-348). Consequence for the kernel: the TCC error taxonomy must be EMBEDDABLE per item, not only throwable — a fan-out of 40 legs where 3 hit a permission error needs 3 typed error objects inside a successful response, not one exception.

THE `open` CALL IS THE ONE UNGOVERNED SUBPROCESS AND IT SWALLOWS EVERYTHING — apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/tools.py:405 `subprocess.run(["open", url], capture_output=True, check=True, text=True)` has NO timeout (it can hang the server indefinitely), and tools.py:407-410 discards the real stderr unconditionally: `return _error_response("OPEN_FAILED", "Failed to open Apple Maps.", "Retry the request.")`. There is no dev-mode gate — the detail is destroyed in every environment. A LaunchServices or TCC denial here is indistinguishable from a typo in the URL.

maps_permission_guide ASSERTS THIS SERVER HAS NO PERMISSION REQUIREMENTS — apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/tools.py:110-111 hardcodes `"can_prompt_in_app": False, "requires_manual_system_settings": False`, and steps[] mentions only Xcode command line tools. It is a static dict with zero probing, and it is wrong for precisely the failure mode that took the fleet down: a folder-service EPERM reading the .swift source, or writing the build dir, needs a Privacy & Security pane visit. This claim must NOT be inherited by the kernel's doctor contract.

APPLE MAPS URL dirflg TRANSPORT CODES, DUPLICATED IN TWO LANGUAGES — apple-maps/src/apple_maps_mcp/maps_bridge.py:96: `{"driving": "d", "walking": "w", "transit": "r"}.get(transport, "d")`. The 'r' for transit is non-obvious (Apple's legacy 'rail' flag, not 't'), and the `.get(..., "d")` fallback means an unrecognized mode silently becomes driving rather than erroring. The Swift side keeps an independent copy of the same mapping at swift:163-172 (default .automobile) — two sources of truth for one concept.

ERROR CLASSIFICATION IS PURELY BY PYTHON EXCEPTION TYPE, WITH ZERO STRING MATCHING — verified by grep across apple-maps/src, tests, server.py and start.sh: the tokens 'permitted', 'denied', 'EPERM', 'EACCES', '1743', 'TCC', 'errno', 'authoriz' and 'System Settings' appear NOWHERE (the only 'permission' hits are the tool name maps_permission_guide). Consequently 'Operation not permitted' -> NOT recognized; '-1743' -> NOT recognized; 'Permission denied' -> NOT recognized. All three land in HELPER_COMPILE_FAILED (swiftc stderr echoed verbatim with the misleading suggestion 'Install Xcode command line tools and retry.', maps_bridge.py:54-58), HELPER_FAILED (raw stderr, suggestion 'Retry the request.', maps_bridge.py:78), or OPEN_FAILED (detail destroyed entirely). This server has the least to unlearn of the seven and is the cheapest place to land the kernel taxonomy first.

TEST TOOLING DRIFT WORTH FIXING BEFORE THE CI MATRIX — pytest is declared in apple-maps/pyproject.toml:29-32 under the `dev` optional-dependency group, but the checked-in .venv was never synced with it: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` fails with 'No module named pytest'. The suite only runs via an overlay, e.g. `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest -q` (6 tests, all passing, 0.27s). P3.6 needs an explicit `uv sync --extra dev` / `--extra dev` step or this server will look broken in CI.
migrationRiskReason: Smallest and cleanest of the seven: a 103-line executor, one command surface, no AppleScript, no Apple Events, no sqlite, no string-based error classification to port, and a 6-test fully-mocked suite that runs in 0.27s with no TCC grants. Two real risks. (1) SHAPE MISMATCH: this executor is 'compile a Swift source on first use behind an mtime gate, then exec the resulting binary with argv[1]=command / argv[2]=JSON, parse a JSON envelope off stdout and a second JSON envelope off stderr on failure'. An osascript-centric kernel that models only 'run this script text, get text back' cannot express the compile step, the -parse-as-library flag, the build-dir env override, or the stderr error envelope — and dropping any of those silently breaks the server. (2) The 15s/20s inner/outer pairing is PER-OPERATION, not per-process, so it is already wrong for the `directions` command (up to 45s of inner work under a 20s outer kill); porting it verbatim carries the bug forward. Everything else — no retry, no output cap, no permission classification, no doctor — is greenfield rather than migration.

framing.notes:
FRAGILITY THE KERNEL SHOULD FIX: only search.py defends the frame. Its AppleScript `on sanitize_field(value)` handler (search.py:390-407) strips return/linefeed/tab AND rewrites any literal "|||" inside a field to " | " before joining. None of the other producers do this — inbox.py:202, analytics.py:705 and smart_inbox.py:361 concatenate raw `subject of aMessage` / `sender of aMessage` straight into a "|||"-joined line. An email whose subject contains "|||" or a newline silently corrupts or splits the record. Two partial mitigations exist: analytics.py:728 uses `line.split('|||', 5)` with maxsplit so the trailing preview field may contain the separator, and search.py:69 uses `split("|||", 9)` for the same reason on content_preview. core.py:159-168 `_sanitize_for_json` normalizes 
 and  to 
 and strips control chars below 0x20 (keeping 
 and 	) on every osascript result, which is why the linefeed record separator survives at all. This is a genuine record-framing concern: a real record separator (e.g. \x1e/\x1f) plus one shared parser would remove five duplicated parsers and a whole class of corruption.

hardWonKnowledge: AppleScript-level timeout injected 5 s shorter than the process timeout — apple-mail HAS the apple-notes trick. core.py:98-124 `_apply_applescript_timeout`: `inner = max(timeout - 5, 5)` then `with timeout of {inner} seconds\n{script}\nend timeout`. Docstring at core.py:99-118: "The inner timeout is max(timeout - 5, 5) seconds, giving the AppleScript interpreter a chance to exit cleanly before the Python-side communicate(timeout=…) fires." TWO CARVE-OUTS THE KERNEL MUST KEEP: (a) core.py:119 skips any script with a line-leading `use ` declaration (ASObjC `use framework "Foundation"` in compose.py); (b) core.py:95/121 skips scripts defining handlers — `_HANDLER_DEFINITION_RE = re.compile(r"^\\s*(?:on|to)\\s+(?!error\\b)\\w+", re.MULTILINE)`. The negative lookahead on `error` is load-bearing: `on error` is a try clause, not a handler. core.py:110-114 explains why: "handler definitions are only legal at the top level, so wrapping them fails with 'Expected \"end\" but found \"on\"' (-2741, issue #63)."

Issue #58 — two-layer defence against orphaned osascript children. core.py:171-183: "1. The script is wrapped in an AppleScript `with timeout` block so the interpreter self-terminates even when the parent process is SIGKILLed or exits via os._exit() (e.g. the orphan-watcher in __main__.py). 2. The live Popen object is tracked in `_inflight_children`. An atexit handler and chained SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers call kill() on any survivors so graceful-exit paths also clean up." The `_inflight_children` set + `_inflight_lock` (core.py:18-19) and `_kill_inflight_children` (core.py:26-42) are the mechanism.

Signal handlers must CHAIN, not clobber, and can only be installed from the main thread. core.py:60-79: "Chain onto any previously installed signal handlers rather than clobbering them (e.g. FastMCP installs its own SIGTERM handler)" — it captures `signal.getsignal(sig)`, wraps it, and re-invokes the old handler unless it is SIG_DFL/SIG_IGN. The whole loop is inside `except (ValueError, OSError): pass` with the comment core.py:78: "Not on the main thread or signal not available — skip silently." A kernel that installs handlers naively will break FastMCP's shutdown.

Orphan watcher — modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk#526. __main__.py:11-19: "When the MCP client (e.g. Claude) exits without closing stdin cleanly, the FastMCP server can keep running orphaned in the background. Capture the initial PPID at startup and self-terminate when it changes (parent died, we have been reparented). `synchronize with` vs `check for new mail` — receive-only vs bidirectional, and the -1712 fire-and-forget contract. manage.py:1338-1356: "Uses the `synchronize with <account>` AppleScript verb ... rather than `check for new mail`. With `check for new mail`, archives done via `move_email` could sit in Mail.app's local cache for several minutes before reaching the IMAP server, leaving iPhone Mail (which reads IMAP directly) showing already-archived messages still in INBOX." When the timeout fires (error -1712) Mail.app keeps the sync running in the background — exactly the fire-and-forget semantics callers expect." PER_ACCOUNT_TIMEOUT_S = 8. Without NSCharacterEncodingDocumentAttribute the Cocoa HTML reader auto-detects the charset and defaults to Latin-1/Windows-1252, so the UTF-8 bytes for ä/ö/ü/ß/emoji get double-decoded into mojibake (e.g. \"Grüße\" -> \"GrÃ¼ÃŸe\"). You CANNOT verify a clipboard paste by reading back `content of replyMessage` — Mail's GUI editor buffer is decoupled from the scriptable property. compose.py:878-891: "The body is inserted via a blind Cmd+V into the compose window, so the window MUST have keyboard focus when the keystroke fires. If Mail is not frontmost at that moment (common on the first compose of a session, when another app holds focus, or when the machine is busy), the paste lands nowhere and an EMPTY reply is sent with no error returned. We deliberately do NOT verify the paste by reading `content of replyMessage` afterwards: Mail's GUI editor buffer is decoupled from the scriptable `content` property, so reading it always returns the pre-paste value (verified empirically — it reports 0 chars even after a successful paste). A content-read-back guard would therefore false-fail every send." The fix is a focus poll, not a fixed delay — compose.py:506-508: "Poll until Mail is genuinely frontmost before driving the keyboard. A single `set frontmost` + fixed delay can fire the tab/paste keystrokes before the compose window has focus, producing a silent empty send." Loop bound is 40 iterations x 0.1 s (compose.py:509-515, 897-903).

LLM callers wrap email bodies in CDATA and it leaks into the sent message. compose.py:136-148 `_strip_cdata_wrappers`: "LLM callers occasionally wrap email bodies in `<![CDATA[...]]>`. HTML parsers treat the opening `<![CDATA[` as a bogus comment that ends at the first `>` in the actual content, so it's invisible — but the trailing `]]>` has no preceding `<` and renders as literal text at the end of the message. Strip both forms so callers don't have to know." Applied on every body/reply/forward/draft input.

AppleScript's `whose` clause cannot filter on message body, so body search falls back to per-message iteration — and that fallback needs a lowercase handler that shells out. search.py:226 "When body_text is provided, we must iterate per-message (can't use whose clause)" and search.py:598-599 "WARNING: body search is significantly slower as it reads each message body." The case-insensitive compare is done by core.py:327-332 LOWERCASE_HANDLER, which runs `do shell script "echo ... | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'"` PER FIELD PER MESSAGE — three shell-outs per message in the body-search path (subject, sender, content). That is a large hidden cost the kernel should know about before it standardizes on a timeout.
migrationRiskReason: The core executor (core.py run_applescript, 572 lines) is the cleanest lift in the repo and is already what the kernel wants — it is the only Python server that independently reinvented apple-notes' "inner AppleScript timeout shorter than the outer process timeout" trick, plus an in-flight child registry with chained signal handlers. But three things make a naive swap dangerous. (1) The `_apply_applescript_timeout` carve-outs are not cosmetic: wrapping a script that defines handlers raises -2741 (issue #63) and wrapping a `use framework` ASObjC script fails outright, so a kernel that unconditionally wraps will break search.py, smart_inbox.py and all of compose.py at runtime — and these are exactly the paths with no unit coverage of the generated script's *validity*. (2) compose.py has a completely separate, undeclared executor: three direct `subprocess.run(['osascript','-'], timeout=30)` calls (lines 557, 964, 1404) plus an untimed `subprocess.run(['open','-a','Mail', ...], check=True)` at line 356. These drive Mail's GUI via System Events keystrokes with hand-tuned `delay` values and a 40x0.1 s frontmost poll; they are not tracked in `_inflight_children`, and moving them onto the kernel changes their timing semantics. (3) Any generic retry-on-error in the kernel is actively unsafe here — compose_email/reply_to_email/forward_email/redirect_email end in `send`, and a retry after an ambiguous timeout sends the email twice. Separately, the error layer is a greenfield rewrite rather than a migration: apple-mail has ZERO permission classification (it recognizes exactly one OSStatus code, -1712, and only inside synchronize_account), so "Operation not permitted", "-1743" and "Permission denied" all reach the user verbatim as `Error executing tool X: AppleScript error: <raw stderr>` with no remedy. There is also no doctor tool to extend — one must be written from scratch.

framing.notes: Framing is an ad-hoc string-prefix convention with a CONFIRMED case-sensitivity collision. The AppleScript bodies emit lowercase `"error:" & errMsg` from their own `on error` handlers, but the executor emits capital `"Error: " + stderr` for transport/OS-level failures (messages.py:44). Three of the four parse sites test only the lowercase prefix, so every osascript-level failure — including TCC Automation denial — falls through to the generic else branch. Verified live by injecting a real -1743 string: _send_message_direct returns 'Unknown result: Error: ... (-1743)', _send_message_sms returns 'Unknown SMS result: ...', the group branch returns 'Unknown group message result: ...'. This is exactly the 'generic failure, real cause invisible' pathology the kernel exists to eliminate. The kernel MUST return a typed result object, never a prefixed string.

hardWonKnowledge: AppleScript `send` LIES ABOUT SUCCESS — the highest-value insight in this server. messages.py:816-839: "The AppleScript `send` command returns without error even when the message later fails (e.g. error 22 for an unroutable handle, or a recipient who deregistered from iMessage), so the AppleScript result alone cannot confirm a send. The authoritative outcome lives in chat.db's message.error / message.is_sent columns, which are populated within a second or two of the attempt." This server therefore polls chat.db after every send (_verify_send_in_db, messages.py:810-891) and refuses to claim success it cannot verify (_report_send_outcome, messages.py:894-921). No other server has this write-then-verify pattern; the kernel needs a generic 'confirm the side effect out-of-band' hook or servers keep reporting phantom successes.

Timestamp correlation is NOT a sufficient key for verifying your own write. messages.py:829-836: "`sent_after_unix` alone is not a reliable correlation key: two sends to the same handle close together (e.g. rapid-fire tool calls) can both be 'the latest row after time X' from either call's point of view, so a plain `ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1` can report the outcome of the wrong message." Fix: additionally match on exact body text, decoding attributedBody when `text` is NULL, with a documented fall-back to newest-row so attachment-only sends don't produce false negatives (messages.py:863-874). This is an agent-specific bug — humans don't fire two sends in the same second.

Error-channel collision between the DB layer's failure dict and a real data column. messages.py:845-847: "m.error is aliased to send_error so a real row can't be mistaken for query_messages_db's {\"error\": ...} failure dict." The whole DB layer signals failure by returning `[{"error": ...}]` and callers test `"error" in results[0]`, so any query selecting a column literally named `error` reports every successful row as a failure. The kernel must NOT adopt in-band `{"error": ...}` result dicts, or it re-imports this bug class into all 7 servers.

`chat id "…"` vs `chat "…"` — documented twice because it was clearly paid for twice. messages.py:955-958: "Group chats are addressed by their full chat id (e.g. \"iMessage;+;chat123…\"). The Messages dictionary requires `chat id \"…\"`, NOT `chat \"…\"`: the latter looks up by the chat's display name and fails for guid-style identifiers (raises -1728 \"Can't get chat …\")." Repeated verbatim at messages.py:1685-1687.

SQLite integer overflow on Apple nanosecond timestamps — worked around by binding the timestamp as a STRING and casting the column. messages.py:1235-1236 and 1251: "String-bind the Apple-ns timestamp to avoid SQLite integer overflow" -> `WHERE CAST(m.date AS TEXT) > ?`. Same trick at messages.py:1407-1411. test_integration.py asserts 'Python int too large' never appears in output. CAVEAT the kernel must inherit knowingly: this silently makes the comparison LEXICOGRAPHIC, not numeric — it works only because current Apple-ns values all share a digit count.

chat.db stores TWO incompatible date encodings and you must sniff by digit count. messages.py:2063-2071: "Older chat.db rows store seconds-since-2001 (10 or fewer digits in the integer); newer macOS versions store nanoseconds (more than 10 digits). Both are handled here so callers don't repeat the heuristic." Implemented as `seconds = ts / 1_000_000_000 if len(str(ts)) > 10 else ts`.

attributedBody typedstream reverse-engineering — pure archaeology, unrecoverable if dropped. messages.py:92-107 documents the exact NSArchiver layout ("the string content is stored after the first `NSString` class marker followed by a 5-byte header (\\x01 <byte> \\x84 \\x01 +) and a variable-length integer encoding the byte length of the UTF-8 text") plus the full varint table (<0x80 inline, 0x81=2-byte LE, 0x82=3-byte, 0x83=4-byte) implemented at messages.py:128-155. Modern macOS leaves message.text NULL for a large fraction of rows, so without this decoder the server reads almost nothing.

AppleScript escaping ORDER is load-bearing, and Unicode line separators count as line terminators. messages.py:48-56: "Escapes backslashes first (so subsequent escapes aren't double-escaped), then double quotes, then control characters... Also handles Unicode line/paragraph separators (U+2028 / U+2029), which AppleScript treats as line terminators." Dedicated regression test at tests/test_integration.py:test_applescript_escape_order whose comment spells out the injection: "Wrong order (quotes first, then backslashes) turns \\\" into \\\\\" which leaves the quote unescaped."

Message bodies are written to a TEMP FILE and read back inside AppleScript rather than interpolated. messages.py:943-959 uses `send (read (POSIX file "…") as «class utf8»)`, with the temp file removed in a `finally` (messages.py:982-988). This sidesteps AppleScript string-literal length limits and encoding loss entirely — the escaping path (_send_message_direct) is only the FALLBACK. The kernel's 'run a script with a large/arbitrary payload' primitive should offer this file-handoff mode.

chat.db's own `total_bytes` column cannot be trusted. messages.py:2099-2103: "chat.db's `total_bytes` is unreliable — many rows store a stale or rounded value (e.g. 1048576 for files that are actually 8MB). When the file is on disk we trust `os.path.getsize` instead."

Defensive row-shape guard justified for BOTH a test reason and a production reason. messages.py:2187-2192: "Drop rows that don't look like attachment-join rows. Two reasons to keep this guard: (1) in tests where a single query_messages_db mock serves multiple queries, foreign rows would crash _shape_attachment; (2) in production, a future schema change that adds an extra column or strips one would degrade gracefully rather than break the tool."

Scan cap and result cap are DIFFERENT problems and both are needed. messages.py:1349-1354: "The scan cap above bounds how many rows are *examined*; this bounds how many are *returned*. They are different problems: a loose term over a 30-day window can match thousands of rows well under the scan cap, and formatting every one of them produces a reply far larger than the conversation it was meant to inform. Matches are sorted by score before this applies, so the truncation keeps the best hits." The kernel's cap-and-disclose helper must expose BOTH knobs and must cap AFTER ranking.

iMessage app-extension 'balloon' payloads must be filtered or they pollute every attachment listing. messages.py:2033-2036: "UTI prefix that flags the iMessage app extension 'balloon' payload format. These are container blobs (Apple Pay, polls, link previews, etc.) — not user-visible files, and parsing them is out of scope." Filter also drops stickers and `*.pluginPayloadAttachment` (messages.py:2081-2094).

Anti-retry-storm prompt directive injected into every permission error — 17 occurrences in messages.py (lines 189, 379, 402, 623, 1798, 1809, 1811, 1838, 1842, 1940, 1948, 1963, 1968, 2004, 2010, 2021, 2026): "PLEASE TELL THE USER TO GRANT FULL DISK ACCESS TO THE TERMINAL APPLICATION(CURSOR, TERMINAL, CLAUDE, ETC.) AND RESTART THE APPLICATION. DO NOT RETRY UNTIL NEXT MESSAGE." A hard-won behavioural workaround: without a terminal directive the agent retries the denied call in a loop because TCC failures look transient. The kernel's TCC taxonomy should carry a machine-readable `retryable: false` flag so this need not be shouted in prose 17 times.

This is a temporary workaround until full disk access is granted." The ONLY env var in the server. It returns a single hardcoded TEST/+11111111111 record, so it is a stub, not a fixture — carry it forward only deliberately.

LIKE-prefilter cannot see attributedBody, so the SQL must deliberately over-fetch. messages.py:1392-1399: "use a LIKE pre-filter on the text column to let SQLite do the heavy lifting for exact substring matches. Messages stored only in attributedBody (binary blob) cannot be LIKE-searched, so we also fetch those and filter in Python." Implemented as `(m.text LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' OR (m.text IS NULL AND m.attributedBody IS NOT NULL))`, with _escape_like (messages.py:1344-1346) neutralising %/_ so a user searching for '50%' doesn't match everything.
migrationRiskReason: The AppleScript executor itself is trivially replaceable — run_applescript is 14 lines (messages.py:32-45) with a single behaviour worth preserving (kill-then-reap on TimeoutExpired) and is already fully mocked in tests, so swapping it for a kernel call is mechanical. The risk lives elsewhere. (1) THE STRING-PREFIX CONTRACT IS LOAD-BEARING AND ALREADY BROKEN: the executor returns 'Error: <stderr>' (capital) while AppleScript bodies return 'error:<msg>' (lowercase), and three of four parse sites (messages.py:1642, 1707, 1770) test only lowercase. I injected a real '-1743 Not authorized to send Apple events to Messages' and confirmed all three return 'Unknown result: …' / 'Unknown SMS result: …' / 'Unknown group message result: …'. Migration must replace this with a typed result, and all four call sites have to move together or sends start silently misreporting. (2) THIS SERVER IS ~90% SQLITE, NOT APPLESCRIPT — a kernel designed around osascript covers only the send path here; the TCC taxonomy must classify sqlite3.OperationalError('unable to open database file') and PermissionError(errno=1) as first-class TCC signals, not just Apple Event errors. (3) SILENT-FALSE FAULTS: os.path.exists() and glob.glob() both return falsey on EPERM, so TCC denials are currently diagnosed as 'Messages database not found' / 'No AddressBook database files found'. Verified live on this machine (which lacks FDA): check_addressbook_access() returns 'ERROR: No AddressBook database files found in …' even though the directory exists and is populated. The kernel must probe with an operation that RAISES, never with exists()/glob(). (4) A SECOND, UNGOVERNED EXECUTOR at messages.py:560-626 — subprocess.run(shell=True, capture_output=True) with NO timeout and NO output cap, reached automatically from messages.py:471 exactly when DB access is denied, i.e. the TCC failure path routes straight into an unbounded, untimeouted shell. Its heredoc terminator is indented (so `<<EOF` never closes at column 0) and its glob can pass multiple files to sqlite3, so I believe it is dead-on-arrival in practice — I did NOT execute it to confirm, so treat that as unverified. It must not be ported forward as-is. (5) The 17 copies of the 'DO NOT RETRY UNTIL NEXT MESSAGE' directive are string-asserted by tests; centralising them requires touching tests/test_db_access_errors.py and tests/test_messages.py. (6) TEST-SUITE HAZARD found while running it: tests/test_integration.py:test_sms_fallback_functionality calls _send_message_sms('+15551234567', 'test message') for real, with no mock. Automation for Messages IS granted from this terminal (I confirmed osascript reaches Messages.app), so on a Mac with Text Message Forwarding enabled this suite sends a live SMS to +15551234567 on every run. test_no_crashes and test_time_ranges likewise hit the real chat.db. The suite passes without any TCC grant only because those tests assert nothing stronger than isinstance(result, str).

framing.notes: The envelope discriminates success from error in-band on stdout, so exit code is not the source of truth. Because there is no timeout, the third case — the child never prints and never exits — currently hangs forever rather than producing any of these.

hardWonKnowledge: THE SMOKING GUN FOR LAST WEEK'S OUTAGE, and it is worse than 'the regex did not match' — apple-events never even produces the EPERM string. Both filesystem probes use fs.existsSync, which swallows every errno and returns false. (a) projectUtils.ts:64-67 `const packageJsonPath = path.join(dir, ...); if (!fs.existsSync(packageJsonPath)) { return false; }` — under a TCC folder-service denial this returns false for every ancestor, the loop exhausts, and findProjectRoot throws `Project root not found within 10 directory levels` (projectUtils.ts:28). Since index.ts:14 calls findProjectRoot() at module top level, that is a startup crash with a message that points at nothing. (b) binaryValidator.ts:100-105 `if (!fs.existsSync(normalizedPath)) { throw new BinaryValidationError(\`Binary file not found: ...\`, 'FILE_NOT_FOUND'); }` — findSecureBinaryPath then returns null and cliExecutor.ts:228-246 emits a 19-line CliUserError telling the user to run `pnpm store path` and rebuild the Swift binary. So a permissions denial is reported as a missing build artifact, with confident and completely wrong remediation steps. The kernel MUST stat-with-errno (fs.statSync in a try/catch, or fs.accessSync) rather than existsSync, and must classify EPERM distinctly from ENOENT. Verified empirically: I ran all 15 regexes in this server against 'Operation not permitted', "EPERM: operation not permitted, open '/Users/x/Documents/repo/bin/EventKitCLI'" and 'spawn EACCES' — every one returns false in both errorHandling.ts and cliExecutor.ts.

The Info.plist linker incantation — apple-events/scripts/build-swift.mjs:58-60: `// Use -Xlinker to embed Info.plist into the binary` / `// This is required for macOS to show permission dialogs for EventKit access` / `swiftc -o ... -framework EventKit -framework Foundation -Xlinker -sectcreate -Xlinker __TEXT -Xlinker __info_plist -Xlinker "${infoPlistFile}"`. Without the __TEXT,__info_plist section a bare Swift CLI gets denied by TCC with no prompt and no usable error. The build fails hard if the plist is missing (build-swift.mjs:49-52: 'Info.plist is required for EventKit permissions to work properly.'). Paired with this, src/swift/Info.plist carries all SIX usage-description keys — NSRemindersUsageDescription AND NSRemindersFullAccessUsageDescription AND NSRemindersWriteOnlyAccessUsageDescription, and the same triple for Calendars. macOS 14 renamed the required key; shipping only the legacy one yields a silent denial. Info.plist.test.ts exists specifically to keep these from being deleted. This is the single most load-bearing piece of knowledge in the server and it lives in a build script, not in any runtime module — a kernel that only unifies runtime code will drop it.

Errors are printed to STDOUT and the process exits 1, so a naive execFile wrapper that only reads stdout on success loses the message entirely. cliExecutor.ts:150-163 handles this deliberately: the catch block pulls execError.stdout, and `if (normalized) { return parseCliOutput(normalized); }` re-enters the normal parser. EventKitCLI.swift:1560-1567 is the other half: outputError encodes ErrorOutput to stdout via `print(json)` then `exit(1)`. Any kernel exec() that discards stdout on non-zero exit will turn every EventKit error into 'Command failed with exit code 1'.

The write-only TCC tier is a real, separately-handled state that most servers forget. macOS 14 lets a user grant add-only access; EKAuthorizationStatus.writeOnly then satisfies a naive `status != .denied` check while every read returns empty. EventKitCLI.swift:1593-1595 and 1618-1620 handle it explicitly ('Calendar permission is write-only, but read access is required.'), and both TS layers carry dedicated regexes for it (errorHandling.ts:11, cliExecutor.ts:79 and :85). The kernel taxonomy needs a WRITE_ONLY class distinct from DENIED, with the distinct remedy 'change the toggle from Add Only to Full Access'.

Two unbounded-blocking hazards that compound into a permanent hang, because this server has no timeout at any layer. (a) EventKitCLI.swift:647-650 — `let semaphore = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0); eventStore.fetchReminders(matching: predicate) { ... semaphore.signal() }; semaphore.wait()` — an untimed wait; if EventKit never calls back the CLI blocks forever. (b) EventKitCLI.swift:1758-1759 — `checkAndRequestPermission()` followed by `RunLoop.main.run()`; the process only ever exits from inside handleAction/outputError, so if the .notDetermined request callback never fires (headless MCP host, no window server to draw the TCC prompt) the runloop spins indefinitely. Node's side (cliExecutor.ts:37-40) passes only `{ maxBuffer: 10 * 1024 * 1024 }` — no timeout, no killSignal — so the MCP request never returns. This is the exact class of bug apple-notes solved with its in-script `with timeout` set shorter than the outer process timeout; apple-events has neither half of that pattern.

Production error sanitization actively destroys diagnostic information, which is why last week took hours. errorHandling.ts:71-73: `return isDev ? \`Failed to ${operation}: ${message}\` : \`Failed to ${operation}: System error occurred\`;`. Anything not matched by the 7 permission regexes and not a ValidationError/CliUserError is replaced by the literal string 'System error occurred'. EPERM, EACCES, ENOBUFS, ETIMEDOUT and every unrecognized TCC message all collapse to that one string unless DEBUG is set (isDevelopmentMode, errorHandling.ts:45-50 — NODE_ENV=development OR any non-empty DEBUG). The kernel's taxonomy must be applied BEFORE this sanitizer, and the sanitizer must have an 'infrastructure error' escape hatch, or unifying the taxonomy will not change what the user sees.

-1743 is matched only by accident, and only along a path that can never carry it. Running the regexes against 'execution error: Not authorized to send Apple events to Calendar. (-1743)' returns true — but solely because /not authorized.*(calendar|reminders)/i catches the word 'Calendar'. A bare '-1743', or an Automation denial naming any other app, returns false everywhere. And the match is moot: apple-events reaches EventKit through a signed-ish Swift binary, never through Apple Events, so the -1743 domain does not apply to it at all. Do not read this server's apparent -1743 coverage as evidence the taxonomy works; it is a false positive on an unreachable path.

`import 'exit-on-epipe';` is the first import in apple-events/src/server/server.ts:6, above even the MCP SDK imports, and exit-on-epipe is a declared production dependency. This converts the EPIPE that fires when an MCP host closes stdout mid-write into a clean exit instead of an unhandled 'write EPIPE' crash. Import order matters — it must register before any stdio transport is constructed. Trivially lost in a refactor, and the failure it prevents looks like a random server crash.

The Swift binary is treated as untrusted input: binaryValidator.ts enforces absolute paths, rejects any normalized path containing '..', does path-SEGMENT matching rather than substring matching against an allowlist (binaryValidator.ts:68-91, with the comment 'Use path segment matching for better security than simple substring matching'), caps size at 50MB, requires the X_OK bit, and in production optionally verifies SHA256 against process.env.SWIFT_BINARY_HASH (binaryValidator.ts:252). getEnvironmentBinaryConfig relaxes requireAbsolutePath only under NODE_ENV=test (line 235-241). If the kernel centralizes binary/script resolution, this segment-matching detail and the test-only relaxation both need to survive.

SSRF hardening in reminder/event URL fields covers the notations people forget: apple-events/src/validation/schemas.ts:53, :65, :77 handle decimal ('2130706433 for 127.0.0.1'), hexadecimal ('0x7f000001') and octal ('0177.0.0.1') encodings of loopback, on top of IPv4 private ranges, IPv6 loopback/link-local/ULA, and cloud metadata endpoints including 169.254.169.254, 100.100.100.200 and metadata.google.internal (schemas.ts:22-28). The file itself flags the residual risk: 'Note: For production use, consider using a dedicated SSRF protection library' (schemas.ts:28).

The text-safety regex is tuned to survive real user data: schemas.ts:12-16 — 'allow printable Unicode text while blocking dangerous control and delimiter chars', explicitly blocking bidi overrides U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 'to prevent visual spoofing', while keeping CJK working: 'This keeps Chinese/Unicode names working while remaining safe with AppleScript quoting.' A kernel-level input sanitizer that is stricter than this will start rejecting legitimate reminder titles.

A dated timezone bug with the reproduction preserved in the comment — calendarRepository.ts:34-41: 'A bare calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) must be interpreted in LOCAL time: shiftDays and formatDateOnly both work in local time, whereas new Date(\'YYYY-MM-DD\') parses as UTC midnight — which slips the date back a day when formatted in a negative-offset zone (e.g. 2026-02-11 + 14d rendered 2026-02-24 in EDT, not -25).' Anything in the kernel that normalizes date strings on behalf of these servers must not reintroduce UTC parsing of bare dates.

Zod generic-inference trap, recorded at schemas.ts:676-678: 'Generic over the schema rather than over T: ZodSchema<T> pins input and output to the same type, which silently degrades inference for schemas that use .default() or .transform() (defaults came back as boolean | undefined, transforms as unknown).' Relevant because every .default() in this server — including the free_slots maxResults=50 that is the ONLY real response bound it has — depends on that inference being correct.

Batch writes are serial on purpose, not by oversight — shared.ts:41-45: 'Runs an operation over many items sequentially, recording each outcome instead of aborting the whole call on the first failure. EventKit writes are not safely parallelizable against one store, so this stays serial on purpose.' If the kernel offers a concurrent exec helper, EventKit callers must be kept off it.

apple-events/check-permissions.sh:8 invokes `./bin/EventKitCLI --action read --limit 1`, but the Swift argument parser has no --limit flag and silently ignores unknown arguments — so this 'cheap' probe actually fetches every reminder in the store. It also, at line 33, probes `osascript -e 'tell application "Reminders" ...'` for Automation permission that the server itself never uses. If this script becomes the seed for the doctor contract, both bugs need fixing rather than porting.

Test-suite blind spot worth recording before the kernel lands: 27 suites / 539 tests pass in ~1.4s and are fully mocked (jest.mock('node:child_process') in cliExecutor.test.ts:32, plus src/utils/__mocks__/cliExecutor.ts). src/e2e.test.ts is the one exception — it spawns `node bin/run.cjs` over a real StdioClientTransport and calls reminders_tasks, reminders_lists and calendar_calendars for real — but its assertions are only `expect(result.content).toBeDefined()`, so a TCC-denied response passes exactly like a granted one. There is no test anywhere that asserts a permission error is classified, and no test for timeout, ENOBUFS, or maxBuffer overflow.
migrationRiskReason: The exec surface is tiny and clean — one execFile call site (cliExecutor.ts:32-55) behind one exported function (executeCli), consumed by exactly two repositories. Swapping in a kernel executor with timeout/retry/cap is close to mechanical, and the 539-test mocked suite will catch signature breaks immediately. Two things push it above low. First, the error contract is inverted relative to every AppleScript server: EventKitCLI writes error JSON to stdout and exits 1, so a kernel exec that follows the usual 'non-zero exit means read stderr' convention will silently discard every EventKit error message; the stdout-on-failure recovery at cliExecutor.ts:154-160 must be a first-class kernel behavior, not an apple-events special case. Second, the biggest wins here are not in the executor at all — they are the fs.existsSync-swallows-EPERM bug in projectUtils.ts:64-67 and binaryValidator.ts:100-105, and the absent response caps on reminders_tasks/calendar_events/calendar_schedule=agenda. Neither is fixed by dropping in a shared executor; both need edits in this server. Also note usesAppleScript:false — this server needs the kernel's error taxonomy, doctor contract, timeout and cap-and-disclose helpers, but nothing from an osascript-specific execution path, so a kernel designed around osascript specifics will not fit it cleanly.

executor.retryStrategy: DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES=2 TOTAL attempts (1 retry). Exponential backoff retryDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1), base 1000ms. Retries only on isTimeoutError() or RETRYABLE_ERROR_PATTERNS match (/timed? out/, /not responding/, /connection.*invalid/, /lost connection/, /busy/, /changed during listing/). timeoutMs is a TOTAL deadline shared across attempts, not per-attempt (applescript.ts:368-374). A retry is skipped unless Date.now()+delayMs+MIN_ATTEMPT_BUDGET_MS(1000) < deadline (applescript.ts:464). Env knobs: APPLE_NOTES_MCP_MAX_RETRIES (=1 restores fail-fast), APPLE_NOTES_MCP_RETRY_DELAY_MS. Sleep is Atomics.wait on a SharedArrayBuffer — no subprocess fork per retry (applescript.ts:183-185). Mutating operations deliberately opt OUT: executeMutationAppleScript() forces { maxRetries: 1 } because a timeout is ambiguous and a retry could duplicate a note or report a successful delete as a failure (appleNotesManager.ts:70-77). jxa.ts has NO retry at all.

migrationRiskReason: This is the reference executor, and most of what the kernel must preserve lives here as behavior spread across files rather than as a single seam. Specific hazards: (1) SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_HEADROOM_MS (5s), MIN_ATTEMPT_BUDGET_MS (1s) and the total-deadline model only work as a unit — applescript.test.ts's 40 tests do cover them, so port the tests before the code; (2) BULK_LIST_MUTATION_ERROR is a string contract spanning generated AppleScript, RETRYABLE_ERROR_PATTERNS and ERROR_MAPPINGS, and the friendly rewrite must still match the retry regex; (3) executeMutationAppleScript's maxRetries:1 opt-out means the kernel needs a per-call idempotency flag or mutations will start duplicating notes on timeout; (4) the framing constants exist in paired JS/AppleScript spellings and the batch scripts use RECORD_SEP as a terminator rather than a separator; (5) the 3367-line appleNotesManager.ts calls executeAppleScript directly in roughly 40 places, so the call-site surface is wide. On the error-taxonomy side the migration is an improvement rather than a risk, but the current state is more subtle than "unrecognized": apple-notes only APPEARS to handle EPERM. I replayed the live regex table against real strings — 'Operation not permitted' MATCHES /not permitted/ and is rewritten to "Grant automation access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation", which is the WRONG remedy for a folder-service denial and would have sent last week's triage down the wrong path; 'EACCES: permission denied, open ...' does NOT match (the pattern is /access.*denied/, and "EACCES" contains no "access") and falls through as raw passthrough; bare 'Permission denied' does NOT match; 'authorization denied' does NOT match the AppleScript table (only checklistParser/noteMetadata check that substring, and only for sqlite3); bare '-1743' does NOT match, and applescript.ts:274 actively STRIPS the "(-1743)" suffix before matching, so no numeric OSStatus can ever be classified in TypeScript. Crucially, parseErrorMessage only ever sees osascript failures: an EPERM from fs, sqlite3, or a failed spawn never reaches it — it goes through index.ts withErrorHandling, which just prefixes the raw message (no detail is swallowed, but no taxonomy is applied either). Finally, jxa.ts (169 lines) duplicates the maxBuffer/SIGKILL fixes but has no retry, no `with timeout` wrap and no taxonomy, and is dead code in the server path (only scripts/jxa-comparison.ts and its own tests import it) — it can be deleted rather than ported. Test suite risk is low: 519 unit tests across 19 files pass in ~1.4s and are fully mocked (vi.mock of child_process or of @/utils/applescript.js), needing no TCC grants; the one un-mocked path is appleNotesManager.test.ts's getNoteLinkById case, which hits the real node:sqlite NoteStore and passes either way by returning null. The 14 integration tests under test/ (separate config, not run here) do need a real writable Notes account and self-skip without one.

framing.notes: No ASCII record separators (0x1E/0x1F) anywhere. Framing is a hand-rolled '|||'-delimited, newline-terminated text protocol built by string concatenation inside each AppleScript, then split in Python. _escape_for_applescript (applescript.py:31-46) strips \r\n/\r/\n/\t and escapes backslash+quote, but does NOT escape or strip '|', so a track/playlist/album name containing '|||' will corrupt the record (fields shift; _parse_library_track_line would mis-assign or drop the row). I did not find a test covering that case. Field counts also vary per producer: library rows are 8 fields (name|artist|album|duration|genre|year|id|explicit, 7 accepted for back-compat, applescript.py:148-181), playlist rows are 5 (name|id|smart|count|time, server-parsed at applescript.py:669-683), playlist-track rows are 7, and search_playlist rows are 5 (name|artist|album|id|explicit) — four different shapes with four separate inline parsers. The slow-path playlist fetch emits literal empty genre/year by writing '|||||||||' (applescript.py:756), which is positional and fragile. Error signalling is in-band via a magic 'ERROR:' prefix on the AppleScript return value, stripped with output[6:] at ~15 call sites (e.g. server-visible ones at applescript.py:792, 1071, 1113, 1146, 1169, 1193, 1219, 1263, 1339, 1381, 1417, 1467, 1542, 1569, 1627); a legitimate value beginning with 'ERROR:' would be misread as a failure. Note also applescript.py:1071 and several siblings call output.startswith('ERROR:') without first checking `success`, so a stderr string is compared for the sentinel.

apple-music/src/applemusic_mcp/applescript.py:49-75 (issue #26) — Music.app stores typographic punctuation (U+2019 apostrophe, curly quotes, U+2026 ellipsis) while users type ASCII, and "AppleScript's `contains` is glyph-exact for punctuation — there is no 'ignoring punctuation'" inside a `whose` filter. Fix: split the query on every ambiguous glyph and AND the surviving fragments. Explicitly load-bearing negative knowledge: "Deliberately EXCLUDED: hyphens / en- & em-dashes. Hyphens are far too common in ordinary titles ('Peek-A-Boo') — splitting on them would shatter the query into tiny fragments that false-match unrelated tracks."

apple-music/src/applemusic_mcp/applescript.py:226-279 (issue #26) — the two-stage track matcher, with a measured cost: "The bulk-fetch is the crux: ``name of t`` *inside* a repeat is one Apple Event per track (~17s on a 12k library), while ``get name of every track`` is one event for the whole list (~0s). Music ignores AppleScript's ``ignoring`` context inside a ``whose`` filter, so the fold must happen in this in-memory loop, not in stage 1." Stage 2 uses `ignoring punctuation and diacriticals` to get Apple's own Unicode equivalence tables for free instead of a hand-maintained glyph list.

migrationRiskReason: Largest and most AppleScript-entangled server in the repo: applescript.py is 4021 lines with 79 internal run_applescript() call sites plus 7 external (safari.py, safari_player.py), and server.py (9587 lines) touches `asc.*` 104 times. Every one of those depends on the exact (bool, str) tuple contract AND on an in-band 'ERROR:' magic prefix that ~15 call sites strip with output[6:], several of which check output.startswith('ERROR:') before checking the success flag — so any change to how failures are represented silently changes behaviour at call sites rather than failing to compile. There is no type checker in the loop (no mypy config in pyproject) to catch a signature change. Beyond that, half the value in this module is not 'run a script': it is 4021 lines of Music.app-specific AppleScript generation, macOS 15 vs macOS 26 AX-path branching, CoreGraphics CGEvent posting with hand-tuned 0.05s/0.3s/1.5s delays, and the smart-punctuation two-stage matcher — none of which belongs in a shared kernel but all of which sits in the same file as the executor. The behavioural risks of a naive swap are concrete and already documented in-repo: (1) a generic retry wrapper reintroduces the duplicate-track bug (server.py:2937-2942, 'that's how the old loop stacked up to 4 duplicate copies'); (2) a broader permission regex reintroduces the smart-playlist misclassification (applescript.py:342-347); (3) promoting -1728 to environmental breaks every AppleScript→REST cascade (applescript.py:376-381); (4) adding an in-script `with timeout` (the apple-notes trick the kernel wants to standardize) interacts badly with the UI-automation scripts here that legitimately sit in `delay` loops for 15-30s. Mitigating factors: the executor itself is one 23-line function, the test suite is large (2236 collected) and fully mocked via a single chokepoint patch on asc.run_applescript, and paths.py already isolates state roots. Recommendation: extract only run_applescript + classify_error behind the kernel, keep applescript.py's script-generation intact, and preserve the 'ERROR:' sentinel contract during the transition.

Risk is medium, not low, for three reasons. (a) The TCC surface is real but non-obvious: apple-weather/src/services/locationStore.ts does readFileSync/writeFileSync/mkdirSync against ~/.weather-mcp, and apple-weather/src/index.ts:63 does readFileSync on ../package.json at module load — that second one is exactly the EPERM-under-~/Documents failure mode, and it happens before any handler or error formatter is reachable, so a kernel classifier wired only into tool dispatch would not have caught last week's outage here. (b) The existing ApiError hierarchy carries per-service userMessage + helpLinks (status pages, NWS outage page, open-meteo GitHub issues) that a generic kernel classifier would flatten and lose. (c) The retry path is dead code today (see hardWonKnowledge); if the kernel replaces it with retry that actually fires, apple-weather will start hammering NOAA/NWPS, which already 429s in production (riverConditionsHandler.ts:201) — that is a behavior change disguised as a refactor and needs load consideration, not a drop-in swap.

executor.mechanism: axios.create() HTTP clients (11 separate instances across 8 service classes, each configured independently — there is NO shared request helper), plus one mqtt.js persistent connection (blitzortung.ts) and one raw node:https request (analytics/transport.ts). No subprocess is ever spawned at runtime. locationStore.ts uses synchronous node:fs (readFileSync/writeFileSync/mkdirSync/existsSync) with no timeout concept.
executor.retryStrategy: Exponential backoff with jitter: baseDelay = Math.pow(2, retries) * 1000, delay = baseDelay * (0.5 + Math.random() * 0.5), maxRetries default 3, recursive re-entry. Duplicated verbatim in FOUR places: noaa.ts:184-197, openmeteo.ts:243-256, openmeteo.ts:840-853, openmeteo.ts:1006-1019. CRITICAL FINDING — IT IS DEAD CODE. The gate is `(error as Error).message.includes('rate limit') || .includes('server error') || .includes('timed out')`, but the axios response interceptor (noaa.ts:90-103) has already converted every error into an ApiError subclass whose message is one of: 'Rate limit exceeded for NOAA' (capital R — 'rate limit' does not substring-match), 'NOAA API is currently unavailable' (no 'server error', no 'timed out'), or 'NOAA API request failed: timeout of 30000ms exceeded' ('timeout', not 'timed out'). I verified this empirically by constructing each error class and running the predicate: all three returned makeRequestShouldRetry=false. No request in this server is ever retried. Separately, errors/ApiError.ts:201 exports isRetryableError() which DOES correctly return true for these (it reads the isRetryable flag) — but nothing in src/ calls it. The retry machinery and the retryability oracle are wired to nothing.

hardWonKnowledge: DEAD RETRY PREDICATE (this is a bug the kernel must NOT inherit, and the highest-value finding here). apple-weather/src/services/noaa.ts:184-197 — `const shouldRetry = (error as Error).message.includes('rate limit') || (error as Error).message.includes('server error') || (error as Error).message.includes('timed out');`. The axios interceptor at noaa.ts:90-103 has already replaced the raw error with an ApiError subclass, so the actual messages are 'Rate limit exceeded for NOAA' (capital R), 'NOAA API is currently unavailable', and 'NOAA API request failed: timeout of 30000ms exceeded'. I constructed all three and ran the predicate: every one returns false. Zero requests are ever retried in this server, in any of the four duplicated copies (noaa.ts:184, openmeteo.ts:243, openmeteo.ts:840, openmeteo.ts:1006). The correct oracle already exists and is orphaned: errors/ApiError.ts:201 `export function isRetryableError(error: Error)` reads the structured `isRetryable` flag and returns true for all three — but nothing in src/ imports it. Kernel lesson: classify on typed error objects / error codes, never on substring-matching a message you yourself rewrote upstream. Also note the corollary risk — turning retry back on will start retrying against backends that already 429 in production.

RETRY TESTS THAT CANNOT CATCH THE RETRY BUG. apple-weather/tests/unit/retry-logic.test.ts asserts only that maxRetries defaults to 3 and that `Math.pow(2, retries) * 1000` doubles — it recomputes the backoff formula in the test body rather than driving an error through makeRequest. Its own header comment admits it: 'The actual retry behavior is tested in integration tests with real API mocks' — and no such test exists. This is exactly how the dead predicate above survived. The kernel's retry layer needs a test that injects each real error type and asserts retry fired, not a test that re-derives the arithmetic.

NWPS BBOX FILTER IS SILENTLY IGNORED WITHOUT THE EXACT PARAM NAMES. apple-weather/src/services/noaa.ts:753-755: 'NWPS API supports bounding box queries via query parameters. The endpoint requires bbox.{xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax} plus an srid; without them it ignores the filter and returns the entire ~13MB gauge catalog.' The working param set is `bbox.xmin/bbox.ymin/bbox.xmax/bbox.ymax` + `srid: 'EPSG_4326'`. This is a silent-failure API: a wrong param name does not error, it just returns everything.

THE 13MB FALLBACK AND ITS TRIPWIRE. apple-weather/src/services/noaa.ts:776-786: 'If the bounding-box query fails, fall back to downloading the entire gauge catalog and filtering client-side. This is a heavy path (~13MB / ~12,700 gauges) and should be rare — a sustained occurrence signals the NWPS bbox query has regressed (see v1.7.1 fix) and needs investigation.' It logs with `securityEvent: true` as the tripwire. Note getAllNWPSGauges() is marked @deprecated at noaa.ts:692 specifically to steer callers off it. This is the axios equivalent of the ENOBUFS/maxBuffer problem — and unlike apple-notes, there is NO cap here: no axios client in this server sets maxContentLength or maxBodyLength.

AXIOS ENCODES SPACES AS '+' AND NOMINATIM SILENTLY RETURNS ZERO RESULTS. apple-weather/src/services/geocoding.ts:11-19: "Axios's default serializer encodes spaces as '+' (application/x-www-form-urlencoded style). Nominatim treats such '+'-encoded queries inconsistently — notably it can return ZERO matches at limit=1 for a query that returns matches with %20 encoding (e.g. 'Clare, MI'). Forcing %20 keeps geocoding results stable across providers and result limits." The fix is the exported `rfc3986ParamsSerializer` (geocoding.ts:20-25), attached via `paramsSerializer: { serialize: rfc3986ParamsSerializer }` to every provider client. If the kernel ever centralizes HTTP, this serializer must come with it or 'Clare, MI' silently stops geocoding.

NEVER ASK AN UPSTREAM GEOCODER FOR limit=1. apple-weather/src/services/geocoding.ts:27-34: 'Some providers (Nominatim in particular) rank or de-duplicate unreliably when asked for a single result, so we always request a small floor and then slice down to the caller's limit. Prevents fragile limit=1 lookups (e.g. the on-demand city_name resolver) from spuriously returning "no results".' Implemented as PROVIDER_RESULT_FLOOR=5 and `Math.max(limit, PROVIDER_RESULT_FLOOR)` at geocoding.ts:457-459, then `.slice(0, limit)` at :474. Every tool in this server accepts city_name, so a regression here breaks all 17 tools at once.

US BOUNDING BOXES OVERRUN THE BORDER — 4xx FROM NOAA MUST FALL BACK, 5xx MUST NOT. Duplicated verbatim at apple-weather/src/handlers/forecastHandler.ts:265-274, currentConditionsHandler.ts:117-126, and historicalWeatherHandler.ts:313-320: 'The US bounding boxes overrun the border (Toronto, Vancouver, Windsor all sit inside them), so auto-routed points NOAA rejects fall back to Open-Meteo instead of erroring. NOAA maps the coverage 404 ("Unable to provide data for requested point") to DataNotFoundError and other 4xx to InvalidLocationError — both are non-retryable "NOAA can't serve this request" failures, so both fall back. Transient failures (RateLimitError, ServiceUnavailableError, network) still propagate, and explicit source="noaa" keeps its error contract.' This is a real permanent-vs-transient taxonomy and it is the one the kernel's taxonomy must preserve: fall back on permanent, propagate on transient, and never fall back when the user pinned the source explicitly.

NWPS RETURNS PLACEHOLDER DATA THAT LOOKS LIKE REAL DATA. apple-weather/src/handlers/riverConditionsHandler.ts:20 defines NWPS_SENTINEL_THRESHOLD = -900 (guards -999 sentinels), and :29-33 documents: 'NWPS uses a year-0001 placeholder (renders as "Dec 31, 1") for stale/absent forecasts, so reject anything that fails to parse or predates 2000.' :41-45 combines both: a status block is displayable only if it has a real value AND a plausible timestamp, otherwise NWPS is returning '(-999 values, year-0001 time, "fcst_not_current"/"obs_not_current" category)'. Safety-critical tool — rendering a -999 flood stage raw would be worse than showing nothing.

STOP BATCHING ON THE FIRST 429 RATHER THAN PUSHING THROUGH. apple-weather/src/handlers/riverConditionsHandler.ts:199-220, with the rationale at :200-203: 'Nearest-first in small batches; NWPS rate-limits (429s observed live), so stop asking after the first rate-limit rejection — any gauge without a series just shows no trend.' Graceful partial degradation beats a failed tool call.

A ZERO-STRIKE LIGHTNING RESULT IS NOT THE SAME AS 'NO LIGHTNING'. apple-weather/src/services/blitzortung.ts:77-80: 'Strikes only accumulate for a geohash while it is subscribed, so a query's real monitoring coverage starts at the newest first-subscription among its geohashes — not at the requested time window. Tracked so results can disclose limited coverage.' The disclosure is rendered at lightningHandler.ts:316-336 ('Explain WHY coverage is limited so a fresh/near-zero reading is not mistaken for' safety), including a '(LIMITED DATA)' status suffix. The mitigation is the startup pre-warm at index.ts:889-897: 'The Blitzortung feed only buffers strikes for an area once it is subscribed, so the first query to a location otherwise reports zero monitoring coverage. Subscribing saved locations at startup lets their coverage accumulate before the user asks. Best-effort and fully non-blocking: it opens a persistent MQTT connection, so it is skipped when the lightning tool is disabled or when WEATHER_LIGHTNING_PREWARM=false.' Two things the kernel must preserve: the stateful-backend coverage-disclosure pattern, and the WEATHER_LIGHTNING_PREWARM escape hatch.

PLAINTEXT MQTT IS A KNOWN, DOCUMENTED, ACCEPTED RISK WITH AN ESCAPE HATCH. apple-weather/src/services/blitzortung.ts:53-64: 'SECURITY WARNING: Default broker uses PLAINTEXT MQTT (port 1883). The public Blitzortung community broker (blitzortung.ha.sed.pl) does not support TLS... allows: Network observers to see which regions you're monitoring (via MQTT subscriptions); Potential message tampering (injecting false lightning data). RECOMMENDED MITIGATIONS: 1. Set BLITZORTUNG_MQTT_URL to a TLS-enabled broker (mqtts:// or wss://) 2. Run a local MQTT proxy with TLS termination 3. Deploy in a trusted network environment. Location privacy: Geohash subscriptions have ~4-40km precision (limited tracking risk).' Env-var escape hatch: BLITZORTUNG_MQTT_URL.

ENV VARS ARE READ AT MODULE LOAD AND CLAMPED WITH A BARE console.warn — WHICH MAKES TESTS NON-HERMETIC. apple-weather/src/config/cache.ts:29-58 getEnvNumber() clamps out-of-range values and warns; apiTimeoutMs is `getEnvNumber('API_TIMEOUT_MS', 30000, 5000, 120000)` (cache.ts:69). Because CacheConfig is a module-level const, an ambient env var silently changes behavior AND breaks the test suite. Concretely: my shell had API_TIMEOUT_MS=900000 exported, and `npm test` produced 9 failures; `env -u API_TIMEOUT_MS npx vitest run` produced 5. Three config.test.ts failures and one retry-logic.test.ts failure were pure environment leakage — the tests read the real process.env instead of injecting config. The kernel should take config as an injected object, not read process.env at import time.

COMPLETE ENV-VAR SURFACE for apple-weather (all read via process.env in src/): ENABLED_TOOLS (preset/±tool syntax, config/tools.ts), CACHE_ENABLED, CACHE_MAX_SIZE, API_TIMEOUT_MS (config/cache.ts), LOG_LEVEL, LOG_PII (utils/logger.ts), NCEI_API_TOKEN (config/api.ts), BLITZORTUNG_MQTT_URL (services/blitzortung.ts), WEATHER_LIGHTNING_PREWARM (index.ts:899), ANALYTICS_ENABLED / ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT / ANALYTICS_LEVEL / ANALYTICS_SALT (analytics/config.ts). Notably absent: any variable controlling response caps or retry — those are hardcoded literals.

THE FILESYSTEM PATH THAT WILL BITE ON TCC, AND HOW IT CURRENTLY FAILS. apple-weather/src/services/locationStore.ts:64-88 — load() wraps readFileSync in try/catch and, on ANY error including EACCES/EPERM, logs and then 'Return empty store on error rather than failing' (:85), setting this.cache = {}. A TCC denial therefore presents to the user as 'you have no saved locations' — silent data loss, not an error. save() (:96-112) is the opposite: it throws a generic `Failed to save locations to ${this.storePath}`, discarding the original error's code and message entirely, so EPERM never reaches formatErrorForUser. Neither path names System Settings, Full Disk Access, or the offending directory. Meanwhile src/index.ts:61-63 does a bare readFileSync of ../package.json at module load with no try/catch at all — an EPERM there exits via main().catch (index.ts:978-996) as a raw JSON stack dump. These three sites are where the shared TCC taxonomy has to be wired for this server; wiring it only into the CallTool handler would miss all three.
